q: The nurse has been made aware of the following client situations. It is necessary for the nurse to initially assess the client who has:
o: Diabetes mellitus (type 1), is difficult to arouse, and has a blood glucose of 38 mg/dL.
A urinary tract infection (UTI), is receiving oral (PO) cephalexin, and reports urinary frequency.
Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), has a white blood cell (WBC) count of 18,400/mm3, and is scheduled to receive IV vancomycin.
Appendicitis, reports pain rated 3 on a scale of 0 (no pain) to 10 (severe pain), and needs assistance ambulating to the bathroom.

key.why: Blood glucose of 38 mg/dL with decreased responsiveness is life-threatening hypoglycemia and must be treated immediately.

q: The nurse has received the hand-off report and is assigning tasks to unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP). Which of the following tasks should the nurse instruct the UAP to perform first?
o: Obtain a sputum specimen from a client who has suspected pulmonary tuberculosis (TB).
Turn and reposition a client who was last turned 2 hours ago.
Deliver a lunch tray to a client who is returning from radiology and has been NPO since breakfast.
Obtain a capillary blood glucose on a client who had a hypoglycemia episode 30 minutes ago and received dextrose IV.

key.why: After hypoglycemia, reassess blood sugar promptly to prevent recurrence of low blood glucose.

q: The nurse working on a pediatric unit has received the hand-off report and is reviewing client data and orders. Which of the following clients should the nurse plan to see first?
o: The toddler who has bilateral arm casts and needs to be fed their breakfast.
The school-aged child who has diabetes mellitus (type 1) and requires blood glucose monitoring.
The infant who has a diagnosis of pertussis and is receiving oxygen via nasal cannula.
The adolescent who was admitted with sickle cell crisis and is being discharged home.

key.why: An infant with pertussis and oxygen therapy needs urgent monitoring due to risk of airway obstruction.

q: The nurse who normally works on the maternity unit has been floated to work on an adult medical surgical unit for the shift. It is appropriate to assign the float nurse the client who:
o: Is being discharged home and needs teaching about dressing changes to a wound.
Is 24 hours postoperative from having an appendectomy.
Was admitted the night before with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
Is scheduled to have an above-the-knee amputation (AKA) that morning.

key.why: A client 24 hours postoperative after a simple procedure (appendectomy) is stable and appropriate for a float nurse.

q: The nurse preceptor is observing a newly hired nurse teach a client who has pelvic inflammatory disease about self-care. The client does not speak English. Which of the following actions by the newly hired nurse requires intervention by the nurse preceptor?
o: Providing written instructions to the client in their primary language.
Contacting the charge nurse to obtain assistance from a facility approved interpreter.
Having a family member who speaks both English and the client’s language interpret the instructions.
Utilizing a facility-approved telephone interpretation service to conduct the teaching.

key.why: Family members should never be used for medical interpretation; a professional interpreter must be used.

q: The nurse working in the labor and delivery (L&D) unit is caring for a client in labor whose membranes just spontaneously ruptured. Which of the following findings is a priority for the nurse to report to the primary health care provider (PHCP)?
o: A maternal temperature (T) of 99.5 F.
New appearance of late decelerations.
4 contractions in a 10-minute period.
Contractions lasting 60 seconds.

key.why: Late decelerations suggest uteroplacental insufficiency and fetal hypoxia, requiring immediate intervention.

q: The nurse preceptor is observing a newly hired nurse care for assigned clients. Which of the following actions by the newly hired nurse indicates correct care?
o: Using a 23-gauge, 1-inch needle when administering a medication in the deltoid muscle.
Placing a particular respirator (N95) mask on a client who has active pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) in preparation for transport to a long-term care (LTC) facility.
Administering oral pain medication to a client 20-minutes prior to hospital discharge.
Teaching a client who has a new ileostomy to empty the ostomy bag 30 minutes after eating a meal.

q: The nurse working in an outpatient care clinic is assessing clients who are waiting to be seen. Which of the following clients should the nurse have the primary health care provider (PHCP) see first?
o: 45-year-old who has pleurisy and is reporting worsening shortness of breath.
15-year-old who reports the development of a bull’s eye rash 2 days after being on a camping trip.
57-year-old who has Grave’s disease and has an intolerance to heat with diaphoresis.
37-year-old who has polycystic kidney disease (PKD) and lumbar pain when ambulating in the hallway.

key.why: Shortness of breath worsening with pleurisy can indicate serious complications like pleural effusion or PE. Priority assessment.

q: The nurse working in the labor and delivery (L&D) unit has become aware of the following clients who are in the second stage of labor and are being monitored with external fetal monitors. The nurse identifies which client as a priority for follow-up?
o: The client whose fetal heart rate (FHR) remains consistent at 132 beats per minute.
The client whose cervix has dilated to 10 cm with moderately intense contractions of 40-50 seconds.
The client whose contractions are lasting 60 seconds with a 3-minute interval.
The client whose bloody show is dark red with active pushing.

key.why: Dark red bloody show and active pushing could indicate imminent birth. Monitor closely for rapid labor progression.

q: The nurse is caring for a male client who has full-thickness burns to 50% of the lower body. It is a priority for the nurse to notify the primary health care provider (PHCP) if the client has a:
o: Pulse oximeter (SpO2) reading 91%.
Hematocrit (Hct) level of 60%
Temperature (T) of 104.2 F.
Urinary output of 100 mL for the past 2 hours.

key.why: A fever of 104.2°F after burn injury suggests sepsis and must be reported urgently.

q: The nurse working in the emergency department (ED) is assisting to triage clients following an explosion at a local factory. Which of the following clients should the nurse identify as the priority for treatment?
o: A client who reports having diabetes mellitus (type 1) and is feeling shaky with clammy skin.
The client who has a large head wound with exposed grey matter and respirations (R) of 6.
The client who has second-degree burns to the chest and arms with respirations (R) greater than 30.
The client who has a closed tibia fracture to the left leg and minimal swelling to the ankle.

key.why: Burns to chest + respirations >30/min indicate risk for airway compromise and shock: treat first.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has severe pre-eclampsia. Which of the following should the nurse include in the client’s plan of care?
o: Administer IV calcium as a continuous drip.
Position the client on the right side while in bed.
Provide a quiet, darkened environment.
Report an increase in urine output.

key.why: In severe preeclampsia, quiet dark environment prevents stimulation that could provoke seizures.

q: The nurse is caring for assigned clients. Which of the following actions is appropriate for the nurse to take?
o: Wearing a particulate respirator (N95) mask when caring for a client who has impetigo.
Having a client who has pertussis wear a surgical mask during transport.
Placing a client who had a stem cell transport in contact isolation.
Initiating airborne precautions for the client who is diagnosed with epiglottis.

key.why: A client with pertussis (droplet precaution) must wear a surgical mask during transport.

q: The nurse working in an ambulatory health center has assessed the following clients who are waiting to see the primary health care provider (PHCP). The nurse should immediately remove from the waiting room and place in an examining room the client who has:
o: A 1 mm area that is flat and red at the site of a Mantoux test that was administered 48 hours ago.
A fever of 101.8 F and is reporting a headache, vomiting, and sensitivity to light.
Heart failure (HF) and reports gaining 3 lbs in the past 3 days.
Myasthenia gravis, ptosis of the left eye, and a nasal-sounding voice.

key.why: Headache, vomiting, photophobia with fever = signs of meningitis, needs immediate isolation and evaluation.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who has a sealed radiation implant. Which of the following precautions should the nurse implement?
o: Place bed linen in a biohazard receptacle outside the client’s room.
Assign a different nurse to care for the client each day.
Keep dedicated equipment in the client’s room until the implant is removed.
Limit each visitor to 1 hour per day.

q: The nurse is caring for assigned clients when a fire with smoke is noted in the nurses’ station. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
o: Move clients close to a window with unit doors closed.
Extinguish the fire starting at the ceiling and move down to the floor.
Use a bag valve mask to move a client on a mechanical ventilator.
Transfer clients by elevator to another floor.

q: The nurse is teaching a class on health promotion and illness prevention. Which of the following actions by the nurse is an example of primary prevention?
o: Teaching foot care to a client who has diabetes mellitus.
Recommending the use of helmets when riding bicycles or motorcycles.
Instructing female clients how to perform monthly breast self-examinations (BSE).
Referring a client who recently lost a spouse to a support group.

key.why: Primary prevention includes measures like helmets to prevent injury before it occurs.

q: The nurse is discussing health screening guidelines with a group of men. It is appropriate for the nurse to state that men should:
o: Perform a monthly testicular self-examination (TSE).
Begin having an annual prostate examination beginning at age 40.
Begina having a sigmoidoscopy once every 10 years beginning at age 50.
Be tested annually for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) upon becoming sexually active.

key.why: Men should perform monthly TSE (testicular self-exam) for early detection of abnormalities.

q: The nurse is teaching the mother of a 9-year-old child about age-appropriate toys. Which of the following toys is appropriate for the nurse to recommend?
o: Board games and reading books.
Large building blocks and balls.
Dolls and wooden puzzles.
Finger paints and bubbles.

key.why: Board games and reading books are appropriate for a 9-year-old’s cognitive and social development.

q: The nurse is screening adult clients at a health fair. Which of the following clients is a priority for the nurse to recommend follow-up with a primary health care provider (PHCP)?
o: 45 years old, has a history of exercise-induced asthma, and has vesicular breath sounds in the peripheral lung fields.
50 years old, has a family history of ovarian cancer, and has not had the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine.
55 years old, has a blood pressure of 164/96 mm Hg, and stopped smoking 2 months ago.
65 years old, has an elevated high-density lipoprotein (HDL) level, a decreased low-density lipoprotein (LDL) level, and does not follow a low-cholesterol diet.

key.why: BP 164/96 mmHg needs urgent follow-up for hypertension to prevent complications like stroke or heart disease.

q: The nurse working in a well-baby clinic has assessed several infants. It is most important for the nurse to suggest follow-up for the infant who is:
o: 6 months old and unable to roll over.
3 months old and unable to switch objects from hand to hand.
4 months old and the posterior fontanel is closed.
5 months old and sleeps up to 9 hours at night.

key.why: A 6-month-old should be rolling over. Not meeting this milestone indicates a developmental delay needing follow-up.

q: The nurse is caring for a child who is receiving treatment for leukemia. Upon entering the child’s room, the nurse observes the parent sitting at the bedside, staring out the window, and crying. When approached by the nurse, the parent states, “I’m so worried about my child.” Which of the following statements is most therapeutic for the nurse to make?
o: “Life must seem very scary right now.”
“I’ll stay here and set with you awhile.”
“Have you considered attending a support group?”
“Are you able to take good care of yourself?”

key.why: Responding empathically (“Life must seem very scary”) validates emotions and promotes therapeutic communication.

q: The nurse is developing a plan of care for a newly admitted client who has histrionic personality disorder. Which of the following interventions is appropriate for the nurse to implement?
o: Utilize compassionate behavior to keep the client in control.
Have the client remain quiet and observe during group therapy sessions.
Work with the client on ways to develop trusting relationships.
Communicate with the client using concrete and descriptive language.

key.why: Clients with histrionic personality disorder need help with developing trusting (not superficial) relationships.

q: The nurse working on a mental health unit has become aware of the following client situations. The nurse should first assess the client who has:
o: Bipolar disorder who is manic, has not slept in 24 hours, and is pacing in the hallways.
A major depressive disorder who was recently overheard saying, “I can’t take it anymore.”
Suicidal ideations and is reluctantly discussing a suicide contract with a staff member.
Anorexia nervosa and has gone to the restroom 15 minutes after eating a meal.

key.why: A client verbalizing "I can't take it anymore" signals potential suicidal intent — immediate priority.

q: The nurse is talking with a parent of a 3-year-old child who states, “I am concerned that my child is in constant motion and is unable to sit long enough to listen to a story. I am wondering if my child may be hyperactive?” Which of the following responses is most appropriate for the nurse to make?
o: “I am not seeing any signs of hyperactivity.”
“It is normal for parents to worry about hyperactivity in their children.”
“At 3 years of age, it is hard to tell.”
“Describe when and where this occurs.”

key.why: Asking for a description (“Describe when and where...”) gathers more objective data rather than assuming.

q: The nurse is teaching the partner of a client who had a stroke. Which of the following statements by the client’s partner indicates the need for additional teaching?
o: “A change in my partner’s voice after swallowing may indicate dysphagia.”
“I should have my partner alternate a bite of food with sips of water.”
“Hesitancy with wanting to eat could indicate difficulty swallowing.”
“I will make sure that my partner has a snack 1 to 2 hours before going to bed.”

key.why: Late-night snacks increase aspiration risk in dysphagia; needs correction.

q: The nurse instructed a client who has gastroesophageal reflex disease (GERD) about dietary and lifestyle modifications. Which of the following client statements indicates the need for additional teaching?
o: “I will avoid wearing tight clothing.”
“I will sit upright for 1 to 2 hours after meals when possible.”
“I will sleep with the head of my bed elevated 6 to 12 inches.”
“I will have a snack 1 hour before bedtime.”

key.why: Eating before bed worsens GERD symptoms. Patients should avoid eating 2-3 hours before bedtime.

q: The charge nurse is observing a newly hired nurse care for a client who was admitted 12 hours ago with pneumonia and has just died. Which of the following actions by the newly hired nurse requires intervention by the charge nurse?
o: Attaching 2 identification tags to the body and 1 on the outside of the shroud (body bag).
Asking the family if they wish to participate in bathing and caring for the body.
Leaving drainage tubes and IV lines in the body prior to autopsy.
Leaving any jewelry on the client to be transported with them to the funeral home.

key.why: Jewelry must be removed before transporting a body unless otherwise specified (e.g., coroners' case).

q: The nurse has instructed a client who has high blood pressure about a low-sodium diet. Which of the following statements by the client indicates a correct understating of the teaching?
o: “For breakfast, I could have a low-fat bagel with organic strawberry jam.”
“For lunch, I could have a chicken breast with barbecue sauce.”
“For a snack, I could have 2% cottage cheese and fruit.”
“For dinner, I could have grilled salmon and broccoli.”

key.why: Grilled salmon and broccoli = low sodium, heart-healthy. Barbecue sauce, cottage cheese, and bagels are often high-sodium.

q: The nurse is preparing to administer a Mantoux test to a client. Which of the following actions by the nurse indicates correct technique?
o: Injecting the medication in the subcutaneous tissue.
Drawing up 0.1 mL of purified protein derivative (PPD) tuberculin.
Inserting the needle at a 90-degree angle.
Using a 20-gauge needle.

key.why: 0.1 mL of purified protein derivative (PPD) is correct for a Mantoux TB test.

q: The nurse has just received a hand-off report and is assessing a client who is receiving a transfusion of O positive packed red blood cells (PRBCs). The client’s blood type is B positive. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
o: Document on an incident report.
Continue to assess the client.
Immediately stop the transfusion.
Administer acetaminophen and diphenhydramine PRN.

q: The nurse is caring for an older adult client who is being seen for a well check-up. The primary health care provider (PHCP) prescribes the following vaccinations for the client: Herpes zoster (Zostavax) Influenza (quadrivalent) Inactivated polio (IPV) series Tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (Tdap) booster Which vaccination should the nurse clarify with the PHCP?
o: Inactivated polio (IPV) series.
Tdap booster.
Herpes zoster (Zostavax).
Influenza (quadrivalent).

key.why: IPV (polio vaccine) is not routinely recommended for healthy adults; clarify order.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is prescribed warfarin for a prosthetic heart valve. Which of the following findings indicates a therapeutic effect of the medication?
o: Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) of 35 seconds.
International normalized ratio (INR) of 3 seconds.
Prothrombin time (PT) of 11.6 seconds.
Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) of 20 seconds.

key.why: INR of 3 is therapeutic for mechanical heart valves (range 2.5–3.5).

q: The nurse is preparing to start an IV infusion of lactated Ringer’s solution for a client who sustained a burn injury. The client is prescribed 5,200 mL of fluid over the first 24 hours. How many mL/hr should the nurse set the pump to infuse for the first 8 hours? Round to the nearest whole number.
o: 325 mL/hr.
433 mL/hr.
217 mL/hr.
350 mL/hr.

q: The nurse is preparing to administer an insulin dose to an adult client. Which of the following actions is appropriate for the nurse to take?
o: Limit the dose to 1 mL when injecting into the deltoid muscle.
Administer the dose using the Z-track method.
Draw up the dose using a 25-gauge, 3/6-inch needle.
Insert the needle at a 15-degree angle.

key.why: Subcutaneous insulin requires a 25–27 gauge, 3/8- to 5/8-inch needle.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is receiving streptomycin for treatment of an infection. Which of the following findings indicates an adverse effect of the medication?
o: Creatinine level of 2.2 mg/dL.
Increased liver enzymes.
Photosensitivity.
Staining of the teeth.

key.why: Creatinine 2.2 suggests nephrotoxicity — a known adverse effect of streptomycin (aminoglycoside).

q: The nurse is preparing to administer prescribed medications to the following clients. It is most important for the nurse to follow-up with the primary health care provider (PHCP) for the client who has:
o: A prosthetic mitral valve, an international normalized ratio (INR) of 3, and has been prescribed warfarin.
Irritable bowel disease (IBD) and has been prescribed psyllium.
A methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) wound infection, an allergy to sulfonamides, and has been prescribed vancomycin.
Diabetes mellitus just had a computed tomography (CT) scan with IV contrast, and has been prescribed metformin.

key.why: IV contrast with metformin risks lactic acidosis. Hold metformin after contrast and monitor renal function.

q: The nurse working in the emergency department (ED) is caring for a newly admitted client who has a history of peptic ulcer disease (PUD). Initial assessment findings include: BP: 110/72 mm Hg P: 90 Yellow colored emesis Frequent belching Hgb: 9.2 g/dL It is a priority for the nurse to:
o: Determine if the client has any stressors.
Prepare the client for surgery.
Administer an IV antiemetic.
Type and cross for a packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion.

key.why: Hgb 9.2 + GI symptoms (yellow emesis) = GI bleeding. Prepare for transfusion (type and crossmatch).

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is in labor and receiving fetal heart monitoring. The fetal heart rate (FHR) is 180. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
o: Continue to monitor the FHR.
Turn the client to the left side.
Assist the client with guided imagery.
Prepare the client for a cesarean delivery.

key.why: A fetal heart rate of 180 bpm suggests fetal distress (tachycardia). First action: reposition to improve oxygenation.

q: The nurse is caring for a pediatric client who is postoperative following ventriculoperitoneal IVP) shunt placement. The nurse notes that the client has become difficult to arouse. Which of the following actions should the nurse take immediately?
o: Elevate the client’s head of bed (HOB) to 30 degrees.
Measure the client’s head circumference.
Prepare the client for endotracheal (ET) tube insertion.
Turn the client to the operative side.

key.why: Difficult arousal = possible increased ICP. Elevate HOB to 30 degrees to reduce pressure.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is 4-hours postoperative after receiving general anesthesia. The client has a temperature (T) of 98.4 F (36.88 C), pulse (P) of 58 with thready peripheral pulses, a blood pressure (BP) of 98/64 mm Hg, respirations shallow with a rate of 26, and pale, dry skin. The client currently has an indwelling urethral catheter with 400 mL of clear yellow urine. The client is receiving IV 0.9% sodium chloride (normal saline) at 125 mL/hr. Arterial blood gas (ABG) results: pH 7.20, PaCO2 54 mm Hg, HCO3 26 mEq/L. Which assessment findings from the box before are related to the ABG findings? 1. IV fluids 2. Blood pressure 3. Pulse 4. Temperature 5. Urine output 6. General anesthesia 7. Pale, dry skin 8. Shallow respirations

key.why: Respiratory acidosis (pH ↓, PaCO2 ↑) correlates with shallow respirations, poor perfusion, and hypoventilation.

q: The nurse working in a pediatric cardiac unit is reviewing the current vital signs (VS) of assigned clients. Which of the following children should the nurse assess first?
o: 16-year-old adolescent who is sleeping and has a pulse (P) of 55.
2-year-old toddler who is walking around in the playroom and has a pulse (P) of 150.
6-year-old child who is sitting at a table eating and has a pulse (P) of 130.
2-month-old infant who is crying and has a pulse (P) of 170.

key.why: A 6-year-old eating calmly should have a normal pulse (~75–115). Pulse 130 = tachycardia needing assessment.

q: The nurse has instructed a client who has lung cancer and is receiving external radiation therapy. Which of the following statements by the client indicates a correct understanding of the teaching?
o: “I will need to avoid direct skin exposure to the sun during the treatment and for at least 1 year afterward.”
“I should avoid close contact with anyone who is pregnant or children under the age of 12 while I am receiving my treatments.”
“I should apply a 50-SPF sunscreen to the radiation area before going out into the sun.”
“I will need to avoid eating raw fruits and vegetables while receiving radiation therapy.”

key.why: Skin treated with radiation must avoid sun exposure directly for at least 1 year to prevent skin injury.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who had a kidney transplant 1 week ago. It is a priority for the nurse to notify the primary health care provider (PHCP) if the client has a/an:
o: White blood cell (WBC) count that has decreased from 6,000 to 5,000/mm3.
Fluid intake of 1,000 mL and a urine output of 800 mL over the past 8 hours.
Increase in weight from 199 to 203 lb over the past 24 hours.
Increase in temperature (T) from 98.2 to 99.3 F over the past 4 hours.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who develops the following cardiac rhythm. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?[A graph of a heart beat AI-generated content may be incorrect.]
o: Notify the rapid response team (RRT).
Determine if the client has an internal pacemaker.
Check the client’s potassium level.
Place a defibrillator at the client’s bedside.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who had gastric surgery 8 hours ago and has a nasogastric (NG) tube to low wall suction. Which of the interventions from the box below should the nurse include in the plan of care? 1. Turn down the suction when assessing for peristalsis. 2. Encourage the use of incentive spirometer (IS) every 4 hours while awake. 3. Maintain sequential compression device to bilateral lower extremities. 4. Irrigate the NG tube with warm tap water as needed. 5. Turn and reposition the client every 2 hours. 6. Place a sign at the head of the bed (HOB) that says, “Do not manipulate the NG tube.”

key.why: After gastric surgery, key interventions include sequential compression devices (SCDs) to prevent DVT (3), turning every 2 hours to promote lung expansion and circulation (5), and posting a sign not to manipulate the NG tube to prevent dislodging (6).

q: The nurse has performed tracheostomy care for an assigned client. Which of the following findings requires intervention by the nurse before leaving the client’s room?
o: There is space for 1 finger to be placed between the tie and the neck.
The client places a finger over the tube opening when speaking.
The tracheostomy cuff can be easily inflated and deflated.
The tracheostomy tube moves in and out of the stoma opening when the client coughs.

key.why: A tracheostomy tube should not move in and out of the stoma when the client coughs. This suggests the tube is unstable and could dislodge, requiring immediate intervention.

q: The nurse is caring for a client who is receiving mechanical ventilation when the low-pressure alarm sounds. Which of the following actions should the nurse take next?
o: Manually ventilate the client with a bag-mask-valve device.
Shut the alarm off and call a code.
Call respirate therapy (RT) to check the ventilator settings.
Assess the cuff of the client’s endotracheal (ET) tube.

key.why: A low-pressure alarm often indicates a cuff leak or disconnection. The nurse should first assess the cuff on the endotracheal (ET) tube to find the source of the leak.

q: The nurse is providing discharge instructions to the parents of a child who was admitted with sickle cell crisis. Which of the following instructions should the nurse include in the teaching?
o: “Restrict play activity to 1 hour per day.”
“Monitor your child’s temperature daily.”
“Avoid areas with low altitude.”
“Maintain a warm temperature in your home.”

key.why: After a sickle cell crisis, monitoring temperature daily is important because infection can trigger another crisis. Avoiding high altitudes (not low), promoting hydration, and maintaining warmth are also part of teaching.

q: The nurse is caring for an older adult client who has dementia and often displays confabulation to cope with anxiety. The nurse should recognize this coping mechanism when the client:
o: Displays ritualistic type behaviors.
Refuses to see family members.
Tells made-up stories.

key.why: Confabulation refers to fabricated or made-up stories the client tells to fill memory gaps, commonly seen in clients with dementia coping with cognitive deficits.
